items.title: Long-Acting HIV Therapy in African Adults with Adherence Challenges.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In eastern and southern Africa, approximately 1 million people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and receiving oral therapy do not have viral suppression because of adherence challenges.
METHODS: We conducted a phase 3b, open-label, randomized trial to compare long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine with oral dolutegravir-based therapy among adults with virally suppressed HIV type 1 (viral load, <200 copies per milliliter) and suboptimal adherence or care engagement. The participants were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive intramuscular injections of cabotegravir (600 mg) plus rilpivirine (900 mg) every 8 weeks, with the first two injection visits occurring 4 weeks apart, or to continue daily oral dolutegravir-based therapy; baseline drug-resistance testing was not performed. The primary end point was a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter at week 48; noninferiority was assessed with a margin of -10 percentage points. Confirmed virologic failure (two consecutive viral loads of ≥200 copies per milliliter) was a key secondary end point.
RESULTS: A total of 540 participants were enrolled across seven sites in Kenya, South Africa, and Uganda; 537 were included in the primary analysis. At 48 weeks, 244 of 268 participants (91.0%) in the long-acting-therapy group had a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter, as compared with 240 of 269 participants (89.2%) in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.1 to 6.9), which met the criterion for noninferiority. The results of a per-protocol analysis were consistent with those of the primary analysis. Confirmed virologic failure occurred in 5 participants (1.9%) in the long-acting-therapy group and in no participants in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.3 to 3.5). Serious adverse events were reported in 11 of 271 participants (4.1%) who received long-acting therapy and in 8 of 269 participants (3.0%) who received oral therapy (risk difference, 1.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.1 to 4.2).
CONCLUSIONS: Among persons with HIV in Africa who have adherence challenges, long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine was noninferior to oral dolutegravir-based therapy for maintaining a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; IMPALA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05546242; Pan African Clinical Trials Registry number, PACT202301600757432TMC278LAHTX3005.).

items.title: Phase 2 Trial of Icotrokinra for Patients with Ulcerative Colitis.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monoclonal antibodies targeting the interleukin-23 pathway are effective in treating inflammatory bowel disease. However, these therapies must be administered intravenously or by subcutaneous injection.
METHODS: We conducted a phase 2b, double-blind, randomized trial of oral icotrokinra, a peptide that blocks the interleukin-23 receptor, in adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis. Participants were assigned to receive icotrokinra at a once-daily dose of 400 mg, 200 mg, or 100 mg or placebo. The primary end point was clinical response at week 12. Secondary end points included clinical remission, remission of symptoms, and endoscopic improvement at week 12.
RESULTS: A total of 252 participants underwent randomization: 63 were assigned to the 400-mg group, 62 to the 200-mg group, 64 to the 100-mg group, and 63 to the placebo group. All the doses of icotrokinra were superior to placebo with respect to a clinical response at week 12, which occurred in 63% of the participants in the 400-mg group, 58% in the 200-mg group, and 55% in the 100-mg group, as compared with 27% in the placebo group (P<0.001 for all comparisons with placebo). The percentage of participants with clinical remission at week 12 was also significantly higher in the 400-mg group than in the placebo group (30% vs. 11%, P = 0.006), as were the percentage of participants with symptomatic remission (46% vs. 19%, P<0.001) and the percentage of participants with endoscopic improvement (37% vs. 14%, P = 0.002). Clinical remission at week 12 occurred in 24% of the participants in the 200-mg group (P = 0.054 for the comparison with placebo); in accordance with the fixed-sequence testing procedure to account for multiple comparisons, no further formal testing of secondary end points was conducted. Through week 28, the percentage of participants with adverse events was 60% in the 400-mg group, 66% in the 200-mg group, 66% in the 100-mg group, and 62% in the placebo group. For serious adverse events, the percentages were 2%, 5%, 0%, and 10%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Among participants with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis, a clinical response at week 12 was significantly more common with once-daily oral icotrokinra at each of three tested doses than with placebo. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; ANTHEM-UC ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06049017.).

items.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide in high-volume metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer: a randomized phase 2 trial.
items.abstract: Combining inhibition of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase and androgen receptor (AR) pathway has demonstrated clinical activity in men with metastatic prostate cancer, although the extent of benefit in tumors lacking homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene alterations remains uncertain. We conducted a randomized phase 2 trial evaluating talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in men with high-volume metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer (mHNPC). Fifty-four patients starting androgen deprivation therapy received two cycles of enzalutamide lead-in before 1:2 randomization to enzalutamide (n = 17) or enzalutamide plus talazoparib (n = 37). The primary endpoint was met, with a 73% prostate-specific antigen (PSA) <0.2 ng ml-1 response rate at 12 months in the combination arm (95% confidence interval (CI) = 56-86%), exceeding the prespecified efficacy threshold (P < 0.001); the PSA <0.2 rate in the control arm was 64.7% (95% CI = 38-86%, P = 0.54 for exploratory comparison between arms). Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 68% patients receiving the combination versus 35% with enzalutamide alone, predominantly anemia (41%). Two fatal therapy-emergent myeloid neoplasms occurred in the enzalutamide plus talazoparib arm in patients with underlying genomic susceptibility. Analyses of paired tumor biopsies acquired at baseline and during enzalutamide lead-in phase demonstrated marked tumor transcriptional reprogramming after AR inhibition, including suppression of proliferation-associated and HRR-related gene expression programs, but without functional impairment of homologous recombination activity. Overall, talazoparib plus enzalutamide demonstrated clinical activity in patients with high-volume mHNPC but did not establish clear additional clinical benefit over enzalutamide alone in this biomarker-unselected population, while being associated with increased toxicity. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04332744 .

items.title: Lonvoguran Ziclumeran - In Vivo CRISPR Gene Editing in Hereditary Angioedema.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hereditary angioedema is a rare and potentially life-threatening genetic condition characterized by recurrent and debilitating swelling attacks. Lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z) - an investigational, in vivo gene-editing treatment based on clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) - is being developed as a single-dose treatment for hereditary angioedema.
METHODS: In a phase 3, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned, in a 2:1 ratio, patients who were 16 years of age or older and had hereditary angioedema with C1 inhibitor deficiency to receive a single intravenous infusion of lonvo-z (at a dose of 50 mg) or placebo. The primary end point was the number of investigator-confirmed hereditary angioedema attacks per month (the monthly attack rate) from week 5 through week 28 after infusion.
RESULTS: A total of 80 patients underwent randomization; 52 were assigned to receive lonvo-z and 28 to receive placebo. As of February 10, 2026, the median duration of follow-up was 7.5 months (range, 4.9 to 12.8). The least-squares mean monthly attack rate from weeks 5 through 28 was 0.26 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15 to 0.45) in the lonvo-z group and 2.10 (95% CI, 1.55 to 2.86) in the placebo group (relative difference, -87%; 95% CI, -93 to -78; P<0.001). Adverse events that occurred during or after infusion of lonvo-z or placebo were reported in 92% and 86% of the patients in the lonvo-z and placebo groups, respectively, from day 1 through week 28. Among the adverse events that occurred during or after infusion and more often in the lonvo-z group than in the placebo group, the most common (occurring in >10% of the patients in the lonvo-z group) included infusion-related reaction, headache, fatigue, back pain, and upper respiratory tract infection. No serious or grade 3 or higher adverse events were reported in the lonvo-z group.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with hereditary angioedema, a single intravenous infusion of lonvo-z resulted in a significantly lower rate of hereditary angioedema attacks than placebo. (Funded by Intellia Therapeutics; HAELO ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06634420.).

items.title: Safety and Efficacy of Acute Normovolemic Hemodilution in Female Patients: A Secondary Analysis of the ANH Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Female patients undergoing cardiac surgery have a higher transfusion burden, yet they remain underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. Although the ANH trial showed no significant reduction in the proportion of patients receiving allogeneic blood transfusions with acute normovolemic hemodilution, evidence regarding its efficacy and safety specifically in female patients remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of acute normovolemic hemodilution (ANH) compared with usual care in female patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a post hoc secondary analysis of the multicenter, randomized ANH trial, which was conducted at 32 centers in 11 countries from April 2019 to December 2024. Of 2010 patients in the original ANH trial, 405 were women and were included in this analysis; 219 had been randomized to receive ANH and 186 to usual care. This secondary analysis was conducted from August 2025 to January 2026.
INTERVENTION: Withdrawal of at least 650 mL whole blood with crystalloids replacement and reinfusion after cardiopulmonary bypass.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the occurrence of at least 1 allogeneic packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion during the index hospitalization. Safety outcomes included intraoperative hypotension, intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, hospital length of stay, mortality, and other perioperative complications.
RESULTS: The median (IQR) age of the participants was 62 (54-69) years. The occurrence of allogeneic pRBC transfusion was similar in the ANH and usual care groups (38.8% vs 44.6%, respectively; relative risk [RR], 0.87; 95% CI, 0.69-1.10; P = .24). Intraoperative hypotension occurred more frequently with ANH (16.0% vs 4.8% in usual care; RR, 3.30; 95% CI, 1.62-6.74; P = .02). Patients receiving ANH also had longer ICU stays (mean difference, 21.13 hours; 95% CI, 1.89-40.38; P = .03) and hospital stays (mean difference, 1.92 days; 95% CI, 0.14-3.70; P = .04). No significant differences were observed in mortality or other postoperative complications.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this post hoc secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial, ANH was not associated with a reduction in allogeneic pRBC transfusion among women undergoing cardiac surgery and was associated with more frequent intraoperative hypotension and longer ICU and hospital stay. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in adequately powered studies specifically designed to evaluate female patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03913481.

items.title: Intraoperative Dobutamine Plus Norepinephrine to Prevent Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Septic Shock: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Chinese Perioperative Septic Shock Investigators for the Chinese Peri-Operative Organ Protection Group
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: International guidelines recommend dobutamine for management of septic shock and cardiac dysfunction with persistent hypoperfusion in adults based on very low-certainty evidence. Randomized trials are lacking on the effect of intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine on postoperative outcomes in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduces acute kidney injury (AKI) within 7 postoperative days in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This randomized, open-label clinical trial in 39 tertiary hospitals in China enrolled adults with septic shock who were undergoing surgical source control between June 2024 and August 2025. Follow-up ended on November 15, 2025.
INTERVENTION: Intraoperative, intravenous infusion of dobutamine (up to 5 µg/kg/min) combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine alone.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was new-onset AKI or worsening of preoperative AKI within 7 days after surgery, defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. The 11 secondary outcomes included Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on postoperative day 1 and urine output 1 hour post intervention.
RESULTS: Among 584 patients (median [IQR] age, 67.5 [55.0-76.0] years; 192 [32.9%] females), new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days occurred in 22.8% (66/290) randomized to receive dobutamine plus norepinephrine vs 34.7% (102/294) randomized to receive norepinephrine alone (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 0.64 [95% CI, 0.49-0.83]). No significant differences were observed in 9 of the 11 secondary outcomes. SOFA scores on postoperative day 1 (adjusted difference, -0.53 [95% CI, -0.98 to -0.07]) were lower and urine output 1 hour post intervention (adjusted difference, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.03 to 1.07] mL/kg/h) was higher in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group. Stage 2 and 3 AKI were lower in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group compared with the norepinephrine alone group (stage 2: 4.8% vs 9.9%; ARR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.26-0.88]; stage 3: 7.9% vs 13.6%; ARR, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.35-0.91]). Tachycardia (heart rate >100/min) occurred more frequently in patients receiving dobutamine and norepinephrine than norepinephrine alone.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among adult patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control, intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduced the incidence of new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days compared with norepinephrine.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06462313.

items.title: Ponatinib-Blinatumomab or Imatinib-Chemotherapy for Adult Ph-Positive ALL.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The outcome of Philadelphia-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph-positive ALL) has greatly improved with the use of tyrosine kinase inhibitors and immunotherapy.
METHODS: In this trial, we randomly assigned adult patients with Ph-positive ALL in a 2:1 ratio to receive ponatinib plus blinatumomab (intervention group) or imatinib plus chemotherapy (control group) as frontline treatment. A crossover to the intervention group was allowed for patients with persistence or reappearance of measurable residual disease in the control group. The primary end point was event-free survival.
RESULTS: A total of 236 patients underwent randomization: 158 to the intervention group and 78 to the control group. The median age of the patients was 55 years (range, 24 to 82). At a median follow-up of 23.7 months, the estimated 24-month event-free survival was 86% in the intervention group and 67% in the control group (P<0.001). Survival with no measurable residual disease was 68% and 42%, respectively. At the end of induction, a complete hematologic response was observed in 94% of the patients in the intervention group and in 79% of those in the control group. After blinatumomab consolidation, a molecular response was observed in 71% and 49% of the patients, respectively. After crossover to the intervention group, 20 of 31 patients (64%) had a molecular response. Overall survival was 90% in the intervention group and 85% in the control group. The cumulative incidence of relapse was 5% and 13%, respectively. As of this report, only 19% of the patients in the intervention group had undergone hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation after having had a first complete hematologic response.
CONCLUSIONS: In this phase 3 trial, a frontline chemotherapy-free targeted and immunotherapeutic approach was superior to the use of imatinib and chemotherapy. (Funded by Associazione Italiana per la Ricerca sul Cancro and others; GIMEMA ALL2820 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04722848.).

items.title: Preclinical and first-in-human evaluation of VG-3927/SAR448851, an oral small-molecule TREM2 agonist for Alzheimer's disease.
items.abstract: Microglial dysfunction is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis, with loss-of-function variants in the microglial receptor TREM2 as major risk factors for late-onset AD. We report VG-3927, an oral, CNS-penetrant small-molecule TREM2 agonist that engages the transmembrane domains of TREM2 and its adaptor DAP12 to promote higher-order receptor complex formation and downstream signaling. VG-3927 and tool compound VG-3909 exhibited (sub)nanomolar potency, cooperated with endogenous ligands including amyloid-β (Aβ), and restored signaling in disease-associated TREM2 variants. In human iPSC-derived neuron-microglia-astrocyte cultures, VG-3927 reduced inflammatory cytokines and markers of neuronal damage. In 5xFAD amyloidosis mice expressing the common variant of hTREM2 (5xFAD;hTREM2CV), VG-3909 induced neuroprotective transcriptional reprogramming of microglia, particularly in the plaque niche; enhanced Aβ phagocytosis; and boosted brain glucose metabolism. By contrast, a TREM2 agonist antibody, which may be sequestered by soluble TREM2 (sTREM2), failed to engage plaque microglia. In a first-in-human, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1 trial (NCT06343636, n = 115), VG-3927 was well tolerated across single and multiple ascending doses of up to 140 milligrams. Pharmacokinetics supported once-daily dosing with high CNS penetration (CSF-to-unbound plasma ratio of 0.91). VG-3927 induced dose-dependent reductions in CSF sTREM2, a biomarker of target engagement, consistent across healthy and elderly participants and participants with AD, supporting further clinical development in AD under the new designation SAR448851.

items.title: Isoflurane-Based Inhaled Sedation in Mechanically Ventilated Adults With Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: The SAVE-ICU Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Rigorous evidence for inhaled sedation using isoflurane in mechanically ventilated patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) is limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether an inhaled sedation strategy lowers hospital mortality compared with usual care intravenous sedation strategy in mechanically ventilated adults with AHRF.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Pragmatic, effectiveness, open-label, superiority, randomized clinical trial in 14 intensive care units (ICUs) in Canada. Adults (≥18 years) receiving sedation for less than 72 hours and receiving mechanical ventilation for AHRF from non-COVID respiratory failure (ratio of partial pressure of arterial oxygen [Pao2] to fraction of inspired oxygen [Fio2] <300 mm Hg) or COVID-19 were enrolled between September 2020 and March 2025 with follow-up through June 2025.
INTERVENTION: Patients were randomized to an inhaled sedation strategy using isoflurane with intravenous adjuncts as clinically needed or to a usual intravenous sedation care strategy. Sedatives were titrated to achieve the desired target sedation score guided by clinical teams and continued until extubation or death.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcome was all-cause hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included ICU- and ventilator-free days at day 30; hospital-free days at day 60; use of refractory hypoxemia adjunctive therapies; delirium- and coma-free days at day 14; and quality-of-life and disability scores at 3 months.
RESULTS: Of 786 patients randomized, 780 were included in the primary analysis (mean age, 61.1 years; 34.0% female; 73.7% non-COVID AHRF, mean Pao2:Fio2 ratio, 152.6 mm Hg); 385 in the inhaled sedation and 395 in the intravenous sedation groups. In the inhaled sedation group, 49.9% to 55.4% of patients received concomitant intravenous sedation on any day during the first 14 days after randomization. At hospital discharge, 161 of 379 patients (42.5%) in the inhaled sedation group had died, compared with 171 of 390 patients (43.8%) in the intravenous sedation group (risk ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.84 to 1.14]; P = .85). There was no effect modification in prespecified subgroup analyses for age, sex, and COVID-19 status. ICU-, ventilator-, and hospital-free days were similar between groups. The inhaled sedation group received more adjunctive therapies for hypoxemia (239 [63.9%] vs 214 [55.0%]; between-group difference, 8.89% [95% CI, 1.95% to 15.83%]) and had fewer delirium- and coma-free days (between-group difference, -0.95 [95% CI, -1.69 to -0.22]). There was no difference in quality-of-life and disability scores between groups.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In mechanically ventilated adults with AHRF, an inhaled sedation strategy using isoflurane with intravenous adjuncts as clinically needed did not reduce hospital mortality compared with an intravenous sedation strategy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04415060.

items.title: Effect of Vasopressin Initiation Threshold on Septic Shock Mortality: The VASSPR Cluster Crossover Randomized Strategy Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: The optimal vasopressor dose at which to initiate a second vasopressor in patients with septic shock is uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of hospital-level strategies initiating vasopressin infusion at a lower threshold vs a higher threshold on outcomes in patients with septic shock.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Cluster-randomized, cluster-crossover, pragmatic clinical strategy trial including adult patients receiving vasopressors for septic shock at 13 hospitals in Idaho and Utah from February 1, 2024, to July 31, 2025. The last day of follow-up for the primary outcome was February 17, 2026.
INTERVENTION: Hospital-level implementation of septic shock management strategies recommending fixed-dose vasopressin initiation when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.1 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (lower-threshold strategy) or when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.4 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (higher-threshold strategy). Hospitals were randomized for the first month to an initial strategy (6 hospitals to the lower threshold vs 7 hospitals to the higher threshold) and then crossed over to the alternate strategy monthly thereafter.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome of 28-day mortality and the key secondary outcome of kidney replacement therapy-free days through day 28 were analyzed using multivariable generalized linear mixed-effects models, accounting for trial site and baseline patient characteristics.
RESULTS: There were 3959 unique patients with septic shock (median age, 68 [IQR, 57 to 77] years; 1903 [48%] were female). Of the patients more likely to experience differential management under the tested hospital-level vasopressin dose strategies (maximum vasopressor dose ≥0.07 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent), 1034 of 1521 (68.0%) cared for under the lower-threshold strategy received vasopressin compared with 651 of 1526 (42.7%) cared for under the higher-threshold strategy. In the hospital-level strategy recommending a lower-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation, the maximum vasopressor dose received prior to vasopressin initiation was a median of 0.14 (IQR, 0.10 to 0.22) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent vs 0.34 (IQR, 0.16 to 0.42) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent in the hospital-level strategy recommending a higher-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation. Mortality at 28 days occurred in 628 of 1975 patients (31.8%) treated with the hospital-level strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower-dose threshold of other vasopressors vs 655 of 1984 patients (33.0%) treated with the higher-threshold strategy (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.87 to 1.06], P = .62; adjusted risk difference, -0.4 [95% CI, -2.7 to 1.3] percentage points). Patients in both strategies for vasopressin initiation had a median of 29 (IQR, -1 to 29) kidney replacement therapy-free days (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.91 to 1.14]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this large, pragmatic clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of 2 hospital-level strategies for second-line vasopressor management in septic shock, a strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower dose of other vasopressors did not reduce 28-day mortality compared with a strategy recommending vasopressin initiation at a higher dose of other vasopressors.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06217562.

items.title: Educational intervention can rewire village social networks.
items.abstract: Social networks shape behaviour, affect information dissemination and undergird collective action. And they can be exploited in the design of interventions in these domains1-7. Although social networks obey fundamental principles, such as the degree distribution8,9, they can nevertheless evolve as ties form and break. Here, through a randomized controlled trial involving a total of 8,331 people in 110 remote Honduran villages, we evaluate the secondary effects of a 22-month public-health intervention1 on pre-existing social-network structure. We used a design in which a varying fraction of village households received the intervention, and villages in which no one received the intervention were used as the primary reference group. In 'low-dosage' villages (in which 5-30% of households received the intervention), people who received the intervention tended to sever ties with untreated individuals to whom they previously went for health advice. Conversely, in high-dosage villages (50-100%), treated individuals increased their ties. These average changes are explained mainly by tie dynamics; that is, treated-treated pairs persist and form new links, whereas treated-untreated ties dissolve. A mediation analysis indicates that absorption of health information increases the likelihood of tie formation and persistence. The rewiring patterns generally lasted for three years after the intervention ceased. Moreover, although the intervention delivered health information, it reshaped friendship and financial ties, not just health-advice connections. In aggregate, the introduction of a new information regime acted as a kind of social institution, rewiring individuals' connections even though the overall degree distribution of village-wide networks remained relatively stable.

items.title: Personalized neoantigen-targeting cancer vaccines in ovarian cancer: a phase 1 trial.
items.abstract: Personalized neoantigen-targeting cancer vaccines in the adjuvant setting are of increasing interest across malignancies. Here we report the results of a phase 1 clinical trial testing the feasibility and safety of personalized neoantigen-targeting cancer vaccines for high-grade epithelial ovarian cancer. 'NeoVax' consisted of pools of synthetic long peptides targeting patient-specific neoantigens admixed with the immunostimulant poly-ICLC, was combined with delayed administration of anti-PD-1 antibody, and was tested in ten patients (one newly diagnosed patient (Cohort A) and nine patients at first recurrence (Cohort B)) with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer following standard-of-care platinum doublet chemotherapy. Nine of 12 evaluable Cohort B patients were vaccinated (75%, 90% CI 47-93%) and 1 of 9 Cohort A patients (11%, 90% CI 0.6-43%). No unexpected safety signals were encountered and no patients discontinued treatment due to toxicity. Across patients, >70% selected targets remained detectable by noninvasive cell-free DNA analysis despite a median of 6.5 months from the time of diagnostic biopsy to vaccine administration, during which, patients received standard-of-care chemotherapy. Biomarker analysis was suggestive of biologic activity of the vaccine in six of ten patients and this was associated with broader tumor and vaccine-specific immune responses in blood and tumor following vaccination. Resistant tumor clones reflected diverse mechanisms affecting antigen presentation, indicative of immune-selective pressure exerted by vaccination. Overall, the interplay between the repertoire of antigens presented by the tumor and the breadth of induced immunity seemed to dictate clinical efficacy following vaccination. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04024878 .

items.title: Metabolomic aging and mortality clocks based on ensemble learning identify systemic aging risk across the human life span in 18,476 individuals.
items.abstract: Aging is characterized by progressive functional decline, yet metabolomic signatures across the human life span remain incompletely defined. Here, we profiled plasma metabolomes from 18,476 participants aged 1 to 96 years across six centers in China using nano-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS) and identified 56 representative age-associated metabolites. In a healthy cohort, we developed a stacking ensemble model to estimate metabolomic age and quantified metabolomic age acceleration (mAA) as each individual's deviation from chronological age. Higher mAA was associated with health deterioration and unfavorable lifestyles. During follow-up from 2019 to 2025, individuals with accelerated mAA showed increased risk of incident chronic diseases, such as fatty liver disease, hypertension, and diabetes, as well as increased all-cause mortality. In a disease cohort, we further developed a mortality-linked metabolomic metric (age deviation) that quantified individualized departures from age-expected mortality risk inferred from plasma metabolites. Age deviation was associated with established composite health measures and increased with multisystem disease involvement and higher multimorbidity burden. Together, these findings support the potential of plasma metabolomic profiling as a scalable, life span-wide approach for deriving clinically interpretable metabolomic aging metrics associated with health status, chronic disease risk, and mortality.

items.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide in high-volume metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer: a randomized phase 2 trial
items.abstract:
Nature Medicine, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04671-5

In the randomized multicenter phase 2 ZZ-FIRST trial, patients with high-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer treated with poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor talazoparib combined with androgen receptor inhibitor enzalutamide had an improved prostate-specific antigen response compared with enzalutamide alone, and spatial transcriptomic analyses of paired biopsies linked AR inhibition-induced suppression of HRR-related programs to proliferation arrest rather than functional HRR deficiency.
